measurements.scope: isolated exact frame mapping/logging; not workload or CI savings

semantics: Native stack depth, frame order, mapped frame fields, metadata fields and all call counts remain unchanged.
Only module-private registered immutable script metadata enables frame reuse; mutable or unknown metadata falls back to the original mapping.
At most 20,000 mapped frames and metadata identities are retained. Cache exhaustion falls back without dropping observations.
Unknown script IDs are distinct from later resolved metadata; changed metadata gives a distinct frame; old snapshots stay immutable.
Owned frame serialization uses checked primitives, excluding inherited toJSON hooks. Mixed legacy and cached frames deduplicate identical records.
Cache membership/capacity are rechecked after freezing to handle nested Inspector notifications.
regressions: Every field, frame order, UTF-16 distinction and metadata overwrite matches the original mapping.
Mutable/unowned metadata and capacity fallback preserve every recorded field.
Mixed legacy/cached input deduplicates identical serializations, including missing URL values.
Inherited serialization hooks are never called when creating an owned cached frame.
Nested freezing cannot exceed cache capacity.
Four 100,000-entry comparisons with 24 frames per call produce byte-identical complete logs.
limitations: Isolated frame mapping/logging timings are not whole-workload or CI savings.
Initial runtime integrity, complete native coverage and complete worker-input ownership remain unproven.
Production engine and Action pin remain unchanged.
